Zero citations for tools/frame_edges/changepoint.py (941 lines), chroma.py (897), gapmodel.py (1267), stepline.py (617), sides.py, roll.py and units.py; vote.py and centre.py are barely touched. They reach the device through session.edge_reader, EdgeWatch (watch.py) and propose.py, whose outputs direct.scan_roll/_hold_to_approved turn into SLIDE commands. Questions: (1) What input do they assume, and what do they actually get? Assumed: dtype and scale, with absolute 8-bit thresholds, and upright un-rotated rows. Actually delivered: corrected 8-bit prescans, uint16 from library.corrected on reopen, prescanNN.tif written in the window's rotation, bottom-up passes. roll.summarise records dtype, but does chroma compare levels across dtypes? (2) Which exceptions can escape? Consider NaN or zero-width inputs, empty frames and ties. Anything other than ValueError aborts a roll (direct.py:3664-3677). (3) Parity with the study. Comments stripped, the diff against research/frame-edge/algos/*_v2.py is about 420 changed lines for stepline and about 390 for chroma, with small diffs for gapmodel and changepoint. Is that divergence intended? Would tests/test_frame_edges_parity.py (FRAME_EDGE_PARITY, local frames only) ever catch it? (4) Can one member alone produce a move, against TODO's 'no single detector may move film'? (5) Are the pitch and width constants really all taken from rps7200.framing, with none retyped inside the members?

How exactly does a library entry name the code that produced it, and is PROTOCOL_REVISION bumped when the bytes sent change? (1) library.provenance() (rps7200/library.py:67-101) runs `git rev-parse` and `git status --porcelain` at save time. That is flush time after close() for debug entries, and FrameWriter time for the GUI. It is not the time the process imported its code. So a GUI left running across a branch switch in this shared tree (CLAUDE.md: 'often has parallel work in the tree') records the wrong commit. Confirm this. (2) driver_dirty is true for any untracked file, and no diff or branch is stored. So a dirty entry cannot be tied to its code. (3) Without git on PATH (common on Windows) both fields are None. (4) Two subprocesses with 10 s timeouts run inside every save, on the writer thread, with the device open. Also check the image sha256: it hashes the TIFF container, so it differs between the tifffile and built-in writers. Does verify or migrate break when the writer changes? (5) Walk `git log -p` on rps7200/direct.py, protocol.py and usb_transport.py from 0f7c21d onward. Do the command bytes sent change without a bump? Candidates: d723896 (the 1.84 ramp changes param_for_mm and therefore the SLIDE params), 622aa5a (byte14_for refactor), 30bad8e and a0de517. The digest has only an info-level note on this. (6) Is the recorded protocol_revision ever consulted by reconstruct, corrected() or migrate?

Concurrency between processes, and between threads beyond Tk calls, has not been traced. (1) Two processes filing into one library/: the GUI's FrameWriter plus tools/scan.py or a probe's debug flush. Within one second they can compute the same entry_id. The scan.json existence check plus mkdir(exist_ok=True) (library.py:166-176) then lets both write into ONE directory, mixing scan.tif, raw.bin.gz and shading.npz from different passes. (2) reindex() (library.py:753-772) reparses every scan.json on every save, O(N) on the writer thread with the device open, and rewrites index.json non-atomically. Is index.json read anywhere it could be half-written? (3) The GUI's full-res and histogram threads (gui.py:3978, 4120) and Save As call library.corrected on an entry that FrameWriter may still be writing. tools/library.py duplicates --delete, migrate-raw --write or migrate-direction can run while the GUI is open and showing or exporting those entries. (4) A second process opening the scanner while the GUI holds it (usb_transport.py:453-470, auto-detach and claim). Does that error path leave either side's device state inconsistent? (5) The Tk thread mutates session.out_dir, out_format and jpeg_quality (gui.py:1580-1582, 1895), and the worker reads them at _deliver time (session.py:2068, 2129, 2162). What happens to frames already queued when these change mid-roll? (6) EdgeWatch generation and version handling against the GUI replacing edge_reader or the survey mid-walk.

Trace disk-full, I/O error and hard-kill end to end across every writer. A grep finds no free-space check anywhere (no disk_usage or statvfs). For each writer, what does ENOSPC or EIO leave behind, and what does the operator see? The writers: tiff.write (tiff.py:167), dng.write (dng.py:145), the gzip in library.save (library.py:192), the debug spool in tempfile (direct.py:666-692), roll.json and survey.json (session.py:1649, 1924), approved.json (gui.py:2943), settings.py (whether its temporary-then-rename write is really atomic and fsynced), the demo's pictures.npz and export.py. Next, after kill -9 or power loss in the middle of a GUI roll and a CLI roll, list exactly which files exist: orphan entry directories without scan.json, a half roll.json, spool directories in temp. Then say what resume, verify and reconstruct do with each, and whether any tool can recover an orphaned spool or entry. Check memory at 7200 dpi RGBI: GUI full-res loads, FrameWriter queue depth, library.corrected float copies. Finally, clocks. Entry ids are UTC (library.py:166) while rolls/<date> is local (session.py:1634, scan_roll.py:291), output names use local %H%M%S with no date for named rolls (session.py:2166-2167), and the roll list uses localtime (gui.py:5215). Check the joins and collisions around midnight and DST, and Windows-illegal characters in roll names reaching those paths.
